item.title: Tailwing 1.0.0-rc.2
item.description:
Tailwing 1.0.0 RC 2

Dictation that always answers. The dictation key is now heard on its own thread, so a busy Tailwing can't miss it, and the pill appears the moment you press. Recording starts straight away, so your first words are kept while the speech model gets ready, and dictation never waits behind a meeting being transcribed. A press that's ignored now says why on the pill: another key was pressed, it was held too briefly, or another app is protecting typing. Settings, Shortcuts tells you if another app may take the same key.

Choose your dictation sound in Settings, Dictation: Beep, Mechanical, Chime or Walkie-Talkie.

During a call, Flag This Moment marks a moment, with a note if you like, and the write-up gives flagged parts more weight. Catch Me Up summarizes the last few minutes, or everything since you joined. After the call, send next steps to Reminders, or with Pro to Things or Todoist.

The brief before a meeting suggests questions to ask, and write-ups have an Open questions section. The calendars already on your Mac are now the first, recommended choice in setup.

Right-click anyone in People to rename them, or to merge them with someone else. Ask is now called Ask Tailwing. Each look's tile shows its name, and the chosen one is highlighted.

A meeting on more than one of your calendars now shows once. Before an update installs, Tailwing checks for a newer one, so you always get the latest.

item.title: Tailwing 1.0.0-rc.1
item.description:
Tailwing 1.0.0 RC 1

This is the release candidate for Tailwing 1.0: everything from the betas, with live coaching, private meetings that name no one, your own shortcuts and one-click AI tools.

Tailwing's own writing model now talks to the app over a private connection inside Tailwing's folder on this Mac, instead of a local network port. Nothing about how notes are written changes.

A fix to how a change of microphone mid-call is reported.

item.title: Tailwing 1.0.0-beta.15
item.description:
Tailwing 1.0.0 Beta 15

Live coaching. Turn on Coach me during calls in Settings, Meetings, and while Tailwing takes notes the side panel shows your share of the talking and, now and then, a short nudge about what you're doing: "Let them finish", "One question at a time", "Ask what they think". Nudges describe what you did, never how anyone feels, and come at most once every 90 seconds. They can also sit in a small floating window.

Nudges follow what the meeting needs. Choose whether a meeting is to decide, unblock, develop someone, catch up or pitch, and change it during the call if it turns. After the call, one private line says how the meeting went for what it needed.

Coaching runs on this Mac only, with the model on your Mac, even if you use a cloud model for write-ups. It stays out of screen shares, notes you share, exports and connections, and only counts are kept with each meeting. It's off until you turn it on. Coaching from Parafoil: for how you change across weeks of meetings, there's Parafoil.

Releases now keep one copy of each download, which keeps updates fast.

item.title: Tailwing 1.0.0-beta.14
item.description:
Tailwing 1.0.0 Beta 14

Private meetings name no one. With Pro, a meeting you mark private is stored with names and personal details replaced on this Mac: its title, attendees, speakers, transcript and notes, the people in the meeting included. Each person keeps one tag, such as [person 2], throughout, and a private meeting stays off person pages and suggestions. In our tests this removes about 97% of names and personal details.

It never stores or sends anything half-done. If names and personal details can't be removed, nothing from a private call is saved or sent; Tailwing keeps it waiting on this Mac and tries again. Marking a meeting private stays free, and without Pro a private meeting is kept as it is and never leaves your Mac.

item.title: Tailwing 1.0.0-beta.13
item.description:
Tailwing 1.0.0 Beta 13

Choose your own shortcuts. Dictation works with any key or key combination you record, including a single Option, Command, Control, Shift or fn key, held to talk or pressed to start and stop. Taking notes, a new note, Ask and opening Tailwing can each have a shortcut too. They all live in Settings, Shortcuts, take effect straight away, and Tailwing won't let two of them share the same keys.

Connect AI tools in one click. Settings, Connections shows whether Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor and Codex are installed and connected, and connects or disconnects each one for you. Your meetings are read on this Mac; the AI tool sees what it reads.

A clearer calendar. Tentative meetings and ones you haven't answered now show, marked as such. Holds with only you on them and no meeting link stay out. You can leave your next meeting out of the menu bar and your calendar out of its menu.

The live transcript model now downloads with the others, so the live transcript works on your next call. Taking notes reads clearly on a dark menu bar. The toolbar looks the same in every look, the Settings tabs no longer shift, and Permissions holds only the permissions macOS asks for.

When you use your ChatGPT plan through Codex, or a model at an address you entered yourself, Tailwing leaves calendar details such as meeting titles and guest names out of what it sends.
